items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: I don’t remember his name. It was earlier. I know it was Dwyer Grade School in Detroit, Michigan. It was Kaniff and Cardoni, they’d sit there right on the corner where that bus went there and all those kids got killed that day. They were going to Hamtramck and I missed the bus by inches. That was the school. For all practical purposes, as far as I knew, Detroit was an integrated city. But I mean, when we went to the theatre I knew that blacks had to sit in the back of the theatre.
Well, it was a mixed reality. There was not a de jour segregation, but there was certainty de facto segregation in certain areas.
